newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana hints at rethink of pula-rand linkage.
newsitem.headline: Botswana hints at rethink of pula-rand linkage.

text.p: Botswana may need to rethink the link between the pula and the South African rand, according to Bank of Botswana deputy governor Linah Mohohlo.

"We are looking to see if maybe we should be doing something else instead of remaining with the current peg and the current ways we have of doing things," Mohohlo told a visiting delegation from Singapore.
Local business is concerned about the impact on foreign investment of the continued fall in the pula which, to protect exports, is tied to the South African rand.
The pula has been pulled down alongside the rand by over a fifth against most major currencies in the past year.

As part of Botswana's policy to diversify its economy away from reliance on diamond revenues by promoting manufacturing industries, the pula is tied to basket of currencies in which the rand is dominant.
Almost all Botswana's non-diamond exports are sold into South Africa and more than 80 percent of Botswana's imports come from South Africa.
Singapore Trade Development Board chief executive Barry Desker said there was concern about the currency issue among potential investors.
"It is no good making money by opening a business in Botswana and see it slip away from you," he said.
Mohohlo said it was important for any exchange rate to be competitive but the central bank was not insensitive to the concerns expressed by investors.
"I do not want you to be discouraged from investing in the country because you believe the rand is going to go down and take the pula with it."
